lesson.title: The Parent Class: Where Shared Behavior Lives
lesson.summary: The parent class, also called the superclass or base class, is the existing class that other classes inherit from, and it is the single place where behavior common to all of its children should be defined.
lesson.body:
When you write `class Bird(Animal):`, Animal is what is called the parent class of Bird. You will also hear it called the superclass or the base class, all three terms mean the same thing, and different books and tools prefer different ones. The parent class is the source of the inheritance relationship: it defines attributes and methods that it is willing to share with any class that inherits from it.

A parent class is usually written to capture whatever is common across a whole family of related classes, leaving the specifics to whichever child classes inherit from it. Think of Vehicle as a parent class: every vehicle has a make and a model, so that belongs on Vehicle, while whether it has two wheels or four, or runs on gas or electricity, belongs on the more specific child classes.

```python
class Vehicle:
    def __init__(self, make, model):
        self.make = make
        self.model = model

    def describe(self):
        return f"{self.make} {self.model}"

class Motorcycle(Vehicle):
    pass

m = Motorcycle("Harley-Davidson", "Iron 883")
print(m.describe())
print(Motorcycle.__bases__)
```

This prints `Harley-Davidson Iron 883`, then `(<class '__main__.Vehicle'>,)`. Even though Motorcycle's body is just `pass`, meaning it adds nothing of its own yet, it still has a working `__init__` and `describe` method, both borrowed entirely from its parent class, Vehicle. The `__bases__` attribute is a handy way to ask any class, directly, which parent classes it was built from.

A single parent class can have many children at once. Car, Motorcycle, and Truck could all inherit from Vehicle, and all three would share `describe` without duplicating it. This is the main design payoff of identifying a good parent class: find what is truly common to a group of related things, put it there once, and let every child class specialize from that shared foundation. The next section looks at the other side of this relationship, the child class, and what it is allowed to do with what its parent provides.
